# Solve a change request

1. Read the issue, approved plan, current workspace state, and repository guidance.
2. Invoke `$reuse-existing-patterns` before editing.
3. Confirm the owning paths and preserve all architecture invariants.
4. Implement the smallest complete vertical change. Keep user-visible UI limited to actionable and task-relevant information.
5. Add or update only tests that protect meaningful behavior, decisions, boundaries, or regressions. Use stable `test-id` selectors for UI automation.
6. Complete the repository-required `$symphony-docs` and `$symphony-technical-docs` impact checks and synchronize all affected functional and technical documentation. Keep no-change bookkeeping out of the issue comment unless it changes how the fix must be reviewed.
7. Run focused checks during implementation, then the task-proportionate repository gates.
8. Invoke `$reuse-existing-patterns` again and correct drift before handoff.
9. Never push a default branch, merge automatically, mutate unrelated work, or expose credentials.

## Report the implementation inline

Symphony stores your final message as the implementation report and hands it to the reviewer and to the independent verification step. Never write the report to a file or end with a pointer to one.

1. Use Markdown with exactly these level-two sections, in this order: `Result`, `Changed files`, `Implemented behavior`, `Acceptance assessment`, `Deviations from the plan`, `Verification`, `Documentation and integration consequences`, `Review notes`.
2. Write `Changed files` as a table of `Path`, `Operation`, and `What changed` that matches the real diff exactly.
3. Write one `Acceptance assessment` bullet per acceptance criterion of the approved analysis, prefixed `Satisfied`, `Adjusted`, `Already satisfied`, or `Not satisfied`, with the observed evidence.
4. Record every departure from the approved plan under `Deviations from the plan`, with its reason, or `None`.
5. Report under `Verification` only checks you actually ran, each with its real command and result, and name the checks only continuous integration can run as pending. Never declare your own work verified.

## Keep the Markdown readable

The result is rendered as GitHub-flavored Markdown in Symphony and in the work tracker.

1. Start with the first required section heading. No document title, no preamble, no closing summary.
2. Use `##` for the required sections and at most `###` below them; deeper levels render identically and only add noise.
3. Never emit raw HTML. It is escaped and reaches the reader as literal text.
4. Put every path, symbol, command, branch, identifier, and configuration key in backticks, and use fenced code blocks with a language tag for commands, diffs, and payloads.
5. Use a table only where this skill asks for one and keep each cell to a single line; use bullets otherwise, one idea per bullet.
6. Use bold only for the fixed verdict labels. No emoji, no decorative rules, no ASCII art.
